prompt: On reviewer-owned disposable infrastructure, choose a small multi-component service you did not build. Produce and test a security operating model from user operation to residual risk. A reviewer will inject one identity/authorization fault and one detection/containment fault without revealing their location. Diagnose, contain, preserve evidence, repair, verify recovery and update the threat model. Do not use public targets, production systems, real credentials, customer data or destructive attack tooling.
deliverables: Scope, non-goals, assumptions and at least three explicit user security promises
Asset and data inventory with owners, sensitivity, CIA needs, retention and recovery requirements
Versioned architecture and data-flow diagram including data, identity, management, delivery, observability and backup paths
Trust-boundary register explaining what changes and which authority decides at each crossing
Actor/capability register and at least twelve concrete threat scenarios covering prevention, detection, response and recovery
Risk register with evidence, uncertainty, treatment, accountable owner, due date and review trigger
At least eight testable security requirements using subject, action, object, context, decision, evidence and failure behavior

Control-to-threat matrix covering identity proofing, authentication, workload identity, authorization, least privilege, separation of duties, secrets, encryption, key lifecycle, segmentation, egress, secure defaults and vulnerability management
Logging and detection design derived from at least six investigation questions, including integrity, retention, access and routing
Incident timeline with first signal, hypotheses, containment decision, preserved evidence, scope, root cause and uncertainty
Recovery proof containing both legitimate-user success and prohibited-action failure plus deployed policy/config identity
Updated threat model, residual-risk acceptance and concrete prevention actions after the injected faults
Cleanup inventory and reviewer-observed proof that every created identity, process, port, file, policy and disposable environment is absent
evidenceRequirements: All work is confined to reviewer-owned disposable local infrastructure and synthetic data
Commands are timestamped and associated with explicit questions before execution
Architecture assertions are reconciled with observed process, configuration and traffic evidence
Authentication and authorization evidence are presented separately
Encryption claims identify endpoints, protocol/policy, key owner and important plaintext boundaries
Authorization tests include at least one same-owner allow and one cross-owner deny
Detection evidence proves a test event traversed collection, rule, alert and owner route
Containment is executed through an authority independent from the injected compromised component
Evidence preservation occurs before destructive replacement where safe and practical
Recovery includes user-centric success, negative security behavior, observability and rollback readiness
Unobservable history and residual uncertainty are stated explicitly rather than converted into absence claims
No screenshots alone; retain machine-readable outputs, hashes or version identities and a written interpretation
Reviewer records fault selection, start/end state and scoring independently from learner-controlled artifacts

rubric.observableEvidence: Bounds the system and ties assets to owners and user outcomes
Accurately maps all control planes and explains each trust change
Produces concrete capability-based scenarios with meaningful coverage
Prioritizes with evidence, uncertainty, impact, owner and review trigger
Builds testable requirements and independent layered controls
Finds the injected fault and separates proofing, authentication, identity and authorization
Finds the visibility fault and proves end-to-end detection routing
Contains narrowly, preserves evidence, communicates scope and avoids unsafe actions
Proves intended success, prohibited failure, rollback and durable corrective action
Provides repeatable evidence and exact reviewer-confirmed cleanup
